ITEM.PTXT: A resin surge tank with built-in electric ACIS (variable intake system) has been adopted, reducing weight while ensuring torque across the entire range from low to high speed and achieving high output.
A 2-way intake system has been adopted in the air cleaner case, and the 2-way intake valve is switched according to the driving conditions to achieve both high performance and low noise.

A porous duct has been adopted for the cool air intake, ensuring quietness without using a low-frequency resonator. In addition, a resonator is provided on the air cleaner hose to reduce intake noise.
The ETCS-i system has been adopted, with a 1-valve type electronically controlled throttle body.
A porous duct has been adopted for the lightweight resin cool air intake, achieving high quietness without using a low-frequency resonator.
The core wire of the porous duct is made of resin, with consideration for disposal.
The air intake inlet has a funnel shape to reduce intake resistance.
Perforated duct. Intake noise is reduced because the holes provide a high sound-deadening effect.

A full-fabric air element, whose filter material uses no outer frame or rubber seal, has been adopted with consideration for recyclability, and the case is a removable cap type for excellent serviceability.
A resonator is provided on the air cleaner hose to reduce high-frequency intake noise.
A hot-wire type plug-in air flow meter with a built-in intake air temperature sensor has been adopted, reducing size and weight.

A 1-valve type electronically controlled throttle body, in which the throttle valve is driven by a motor, has been adopted, and the bore diameter has been increased and optimized to handle the high output of the engine.
The accelerator position sensor is located on the accelerator pedal, making the system linkless.

The driver's operation (accelerator pedal depression amount) is transmitted to the engine control computer by the accelerator position sensor located on the accelerator pedal. The engine control computer determines the throttle opening appropriate to the driving conditions and drives the electronic throttle motor. The throttle valve opening is fed back to the engine control computer by the throttle position sensor.

A DC motor with good response and low power consumption is used for the throttle valve drive motor, and a non-contact type throttle sensor has been adopted, achieving a lightweight and compact construction.
The insides of both the accelerator position sensor and the throttle position sensor have a 2-system (main and sub) configuration, and the system is constantly monitored for malfunctions.

If a malfunction is detected, the warning light in the meter alerts the driver and current to the motor is cut. The throttle valve is returned to a predetermined opening by the throttle valve return spring. Engine output is adjusted according to the accelerator opening through fuel injection cut and ignition retard, enabling the vehicle to be driven.

A compact, lightweight plastic hot-wire type plug-in air flow meter has been adopted. Accordingly, the air cleaner is mounted above the transmission and has been downsized, reducing weight and making it more compact.

The hot-wire type plug-in air flow meter passes part of the intake air through the detection section and directly measures the mass flow rate, improving detection accuracy and reducing intake resistance.

A bypass flow measurement method, which is less affected by intake pulsation from the engine, has been adopted. Also, low loss is achieved by a flow passage structure with low fluid resistance, allowing air volumes from small to large to be measured reliably.

MECA.TITLE: Hot-wire Type Air Flow Meter Operation

ITEM.PTXT: Part of the intake air is bypassed and the intake air volume is measured at the hot wire measuring section. The hot wire measuring section uses a platinum filament (platinum hot wire), and a bridge circuit is formed by the hot wires of the intake air temperature measuring resistor and the heating resistor (heater) to measure the engine intake air volume. Due to the characteristics of the hot-wire type air flow meter, the mass flow rate can in principle be measured directly, so density correction for changes in intake air temperature is not necessary; however, intake air temperature information is required for engine controls such as EFI. Therefore, a compact thermistor type intake air temperature sensor is built into the air flow meter to detect the intake air temperature.

When the intake air volume changes, the bridge circuit of the hot wire measuring section feedback-controls the power supplied to the heating resistor so that the temperature difference between the intake air temperature measuring resistor and the heating resistor (heater) is always kept constant. This supplied power is converted into a voltage and output to the engine control computer. The engine control computer calculates the engine intake air volume from the predetermined relationship between the air flow meter output voltage and flow rate.

Electric ACIS (Acoustic Control Induction System) has been adopted and integrated into the resin surge tank by laser welding, reducing the number of parts and weight.

The engine control computer electrically opens and closes the ACIS valve in accordance with the engine speed, throttle valve opening and the cycle of the pulsating flow that changes with engine speed, switching the intake pipe length to increase engine torque.

Pressure fluctuations occur in the intake pipe due to the intermittent intake strokes. The effect that pressure fluctuations remaining in the intake pipe after the intake valve closes have on the next intake stroke is called the pulsation effect. When the pressure fluctuation remaining after the intake valve closes is synchronized with the next intake stroke, the pressure at valve opening becomes higher, so the intake air volume increases and torque can be increased.

To actively utilize this pulsation effect, the variable intake system switches the effective intake pipe length in 2 stages in accordance with the cycle of the pulsating flow that changes with engine speed, increasing torque across the entire range.
